title: KL-regularized policies and reward exploitation
outcome: Derive an exact finite-policy optimum and show why improving a proxy reward can reduce independently defined task utility.

exercises.title: Add a reward constant
exercises.hint: The common exponential factor cancels in normalization.
exercises.answer: Only relative action rewards influence the finite-policy optimum under a fixed reference.

exercises.title: Rescale reward and beta
exercises.answer: The objective scale changes but the reward-to-regularization tradeoff does not.

exercises.title: Inspect the gradient sum
exercises.hint: A common logit shift leaves softmax probabilities unchanged.
exercises.answer: This invariance checks the centered gradient through the probability parameterization.

exercises.title: Handle large rewards
exercises.hint: Subtract the maximum log weight before exponentiation.
exercises.answer: The subtraction preserves normalized ratios while avoiding unnecessary overflow.

exercises.title: Identify missing support
exercises.task: Give a useful action zero reference probability.
exercises.expected: The bounded helper rejects the unsupported objective.
exercises.hint: KL in this direction is infinite for positive mass outside reference support.
exercises.answer: Adding a probability floor creates another reference distribution and must be treated as a modeling change.

exercises.title: Test independent utility
exercises.task: Optimize the authored proxy from case B.
exercises.expected: Proxy reward rises while independent task utility falls.
exercises.hint: Keep the evaluation utility outside the training objective.
exercises.answer: KL regularization can limit distribution change, but it cannot validate the reward model or rule out exploitation of a proxy.

sources: DPO derivation of the regularized policy
